Nothing on the glass jumps any more, and four things seen on the first live screens.

- **Every change of state slides.** When the hour or the phase changes, every colour the interface takes from the state moves over the turn (840 ms) instead of switching; the seams still flash Bone first. The curtain itself never jumps either: before it is recut or recoloured, what it looks like now is copied to a ghost layer and faded out under the new glass while the new glass fades in. A rebuild that changes nothing repaints nothing.
- **Foundry's tiles are enclosed in their shard.** The side strip is now at least as wide and as long as the tiles it carries, and the mid seam sits below their shard, so a GM's full column of sidebar tabs and both columns of scene controls stay on the glass. The blocks' rotation is written as a stylesheet rule, not an inline style, so a block the module rebuilds from scratch (the status strip, the Event panel) keeps its pane's angle.
- **The scene navigation leaves the clock.** Under the theme the scene list under the clock is hidden; the GM changes scenes from the sidebar's Scenes tab, which the theme shows again for the GM.
- **The GM launcher has its own pane again** (a block that merely touches its neighbour no longer shares the neighbour's pane).
- **The Projects tray** wears the rail's face (the chrome font, or the pixel font when that setting is on) and is as tall as the clock's block, so the two top corners of the glass weigh the same.
- **Window glass matches the curtain**: the same share of coloured panes on a title band as on the curtain, half the inner glow, a darker band.
